# aidial_application (Resource)

Manages an application in DIAL Core (`PUT /v1/applications/{bucket}/{path}`). An application is either endpoint-based (`endpoint`) or schema-based (`application_type_schema_id` with `application_properties`); DIAL Core rejects both together. Code-based applications (`function`), `mcp`, `routes` and `external_services` are not managed: a PUT replaces the whole document, so they are dropped on the next apply.

## Example Usage

```terraform
# An endpoint-based application.
resource "aidial_application" "example" {
  bucket       = "platform"
  path         = "my-application"
  display_name = "Support assistant"
  description  = "Answers questions about the product"
  endpoint     = "https://application.example.invalid/chat"

  forward_auth_token = true
  max_retry_attempts = 2
  interceptors       = ["my-interceptor"]

  default_headers = {
    "X-Team" = "platform"
  }
}

# A schema-based application: no endpoint, typed by an application type schema.
resource "aidial_application" "typed" {
  bucket                     = "platform"
  path                       = "my-typed-application"
  application_type_schema_id = aidial_application_type_schema.example.schema_id

  application_properties = {
    prompt = "You are a helpful assistant."
  }
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `bucket` (String) Target DIAL bucket, for example `platform` or `public`.
- `path` (String) Application path inside the bucket. `/` separates folders; DIAL Core accepts `/` only in the `public` bucket.

### Optional

- `application_properties` (Dynamic) Values for the properties of the application type schema (free-form object, sent to DIAL as-is).
- `application_type_schema_id` (String) URI (`$id`) of the application type schema, for example the `schema_id` of an `aidial_application_type_schema`. Schema-based applications take no `endpoint`.
- `catalog_properties` (Dynamic) Catalog metadata of the application (free-form object).
- `catalog_schema_id` (String) URI (`$id`) of the catalog schema describing `catalog_properties`, for example the `schema_id` of an `aidial_catalog_schema`.
- `default_headers` (Map of String) Additional headers sent with every request to the application's endpoint.
- `defaults` (Dynamic) Default request parameters (free-form object, sent to DIAL as-is).
- `description` (String) Application description.
- `display_name` (String) Human-readable application name.
- `display_version` (String) Version shown for the application.
- `editor_url` (String) URL of the application editor.
- `endpoint` (String) URL DIAL Core calls to run the application. Set exactly one of `endpoint` and `application_type_schema_id`.
- `features` (Attributes) (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--features))
- `forward_auth_token` (Boolean) Forward the caller's authorization token to the application. DIAL Core defaults to false.
- `icon_url` (String) URL of the application icon.
- `interceptors` (Set of String) Names of interceptors applied to the application's requests. DIAL Core defaults to none.
- `interfaces` (Attributes Map) Per-interface deployment configuration, keyed by DIAL Core interface type: `openaiChatCompletions`, `openaiEmbeddings`, `openaiResponses`, `anthropicMessages`. The keys are Core's camelCase names and are sent as written; the attributes inside each entry use snake_case. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--interfaces))
- `max_retry_attempts` (Number) Maximum number of retry attempts. DIAL Core defaults to 1.
- `name` (String) Application name sent in the DIAL API request body. DIAL Core derives the name from the bucket and path, so it can be omitted; then it is read back from the API.
- `user_roles` (Set of String) Roles allowed to use the application.
- `viewer_url` (String) URL of the application viewer.

### Read-Only

- `api_name` (String) Canonical application name returned by the DIAL API.
- `id` (String) Resource identifier in the form <bucket>/<path>.

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

In Terraform v1.5.0 and later, the [`import` block](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/language/import) can be used with the `id` attribute, for example:

```terraform
import {
  to = aidial_application.example
  id = "platform/my-application"
}
```

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
# Import by <bucket>/<path>. The bucket is "platform" or "public"; the path may contain "/".
terraform import aidial_application.example platform/my-application
```
